name: vignette-street
street_identity: Quay Street, in the Hook. Ruled by Jafar 2026-09-08 (D15 amendment, option C). The piece identifiers in vignette-pieces.json are all east_parade_*, and those are ASSET NAMES minted before this street had a district: they carry no claim about where it is and are deliberately not renamed, because renaming them would break the bill of materials, the golden rows and every verdict key that has ever named a piece. The player's pub, Mickey's, stands on this street.
scope: The D1b street vignette and nothing else, per game-design/decision-D1b-rescope.md.
law: THIS FILE IS THE SCENE. Every object in either engine arrives via that engine's generator reading THIS file. A hand-placed object, a hand-edited binary scene or a hand-edited uasset disqualifies the still as D1b evidence, so a dimension that is not here may not be invented in an emitter.
bill_of_materials: production/specs/vignette-bill-of-materials.json. Every emitted piece carries the id of the BOM line that authorises it; the 26 lines with make_by=PROC are the ones this file drives.

period.note: Late analog Britain. Landlines, cash, paper. Nothing on this street may imply a hand-held telephone, a computer network of any kind, a wheeled refuse bin, or blister tactile paving, whose introduction date is unverified and which the BOM excludes for that reason.

frame.x: along the street. 0 at the south end, +x north. cam_A looks up +x.
frame.y: up. y=0 is the carriageway CROWN at the centreline, so the channel is below zero and the footway above it. Every other level in this file is derived from the section by the generator, never written twice.
frame.z: across the street. z=0 is the crown. +z is the EAST side, which carries the shop frontage. -z is the WEST side, which cam_B stands on.
frame.yaw_deg: compass-style about +y, measured from +x. 0 faces +x, 90 faces +z. Each engine converts to its own convention in its emitter and nowhere else.
frame.pitch_deg: positive is DOWN, matching the RefTour convention already in SimDirector.
frame.handedness_note: This frame is engine-neutral on purpose. Unity is Y-up left-handed metres and Unreal is Z-up left-handed centimetres, so both emitters convert on read. Writing the scene in either engine's native frame would make the other emitter the one that carries the error.

dimension_provenance.what: Where each class of number in this file comes from, because a plausible number with no provenance is the thing rule 2 exists to stop.
dimension_provenance.derived: Computed in this file's notes from a stated physical fact: the sodium colour, the sun elevation, the aerial element length, the brick course, the two camera pitches, every level in the street section. Read the note beside the number.
dimension_provenance.measured: Copied from a measurement already printed in this repository, with the source named: the 0.40 m gully grate and the 5 to 6 m lighting column both come from production/specs/vignette-bill-of-materials.json.
dimension_provenance.trade_standard: British building and highway trade sizes recalled and NOT verified against BS 7263, BS 5489 or the Design Manual for Roads and Bridges from this container, which has no access to them. Every one is flagged trade_standard in its note. They are the class of number most likely to be wrong, and the instrument that settles them is an eye check on the committed still by someone who has stood on a British pavement, which is a named next step and not a claim made here.
dimension_provenance.judgement: Composition choices with no right answer: street length, how many bays, where the kiosk stands. Flagged judgement in the note. Changing one changes the picture and no gate.

street.length_note: judgement. Long enough that cam_A has a kerb line running to a vanishing point through the fog, short enough that the whole vignette is one dispatch. The blocks occupy 3.0 to 39.0, so the road runs past them at both ends and the frame has no visible edge of the world. LENGTHENED 24 September from 42.0 to 48.0 for the ship chandler's, which stands 40.0 to 46.0, so the road still runs past the blocks at both ends.

carriageway.note: trade_standard. Two 3.0 m lanes is the common British two-way residential carriageway; 6.0 m overall is a narrow shopping parade rather than a distributor road. The crossfall is 1 in 40, the value British road practice uses for a straight carriageway. DERIVED CONSEQUENCE: the crown stands 3.0 x 0.025 = 0.075 m above the channel, and that 75 mm is the whole reason A0 exists. A flat carriageway puts the wet-condition water everywhere instead of at the kerb.

channel.note: trade_standard. The channel course beside the kerb, 255 mm wide, laid at the same crossfall as the carriageway and in the kerb's own concrete rather than asphalt. It is the strip the gutter water runs in and it reads as a different material in every British street photograph.

kerb.note: trade_standard. 125 mm face is the standard British kerb upstand; the block is 125 x 255 in section and 915 mm long, which is why a British kerb line has a joint every 915 mm and an American one does not. The face is emitted SQUARE, not half-battered: the batter is a chamfer of about 12 mm over the top 50 mm of the face and it is the named next rung, deliberately absent here rather than approximated, because a field in this file that the emitter ignores would be a lie about what the still shows.

dropped_kerb.note: trade_standard for the 6 mm flush upstand, which is the maximum a dropped crossing is allowed to leave. The condition B2 requires is met by the YARD ENTRANCE between the two west blocks, which sits at this x: the gap in the terrace and the drop in the kerb are the same event, and neither is placed independently of the other. taper_blocks is how many 915 mm kerbs are used to climb back to full upstand on each side.

gully.note: MEASURED. 0.40 m is the measured footprint of drainage_grate_01 quoted in the bill of materials (0.40 x 0.40 x 0.01 m), so the recess is cut to the grate rather than the grate scaled to a recess. recess_depth is how far the kerb top drops over that 0.40 m; dish_depth is how far the channel sinks under the grate. The grate itself is BOM line A7, route HAVE, and is NOT emitted by this file: the recess exists so that when the prop is dropped in it is not a sticker on an unbroken kerb line.

footway.note: trade_standard. 2.0 m is the normal British footway width; the crossfall falls TOWARD the road at 1 in 40 so surface water reaches the channel. DERIVED CONSEQUENCE: the back of the footway stands 2.0 x 0.025 = 0.050 m above its kerb edge, and the kerb edge stands 0.125 m above the channel, so the building threshold is 0.100 m above the crown of the road. The pavement being at a different level from the road is the entire second half of A0 and it is 100 mm, not a metre.

roof.note: trade_standard. 35 degrees is the common British slated terrace pitch and sits clear of the roughly 25 to 30 degree minimum a slate covering needs to stay watertight. DERIVED: the ridge runs along the street and stands depth/2 x tan(35) = 4.0 x 0.7002 = 2.80 m above the eaves.

blocks.note: judgement on 6 bays at 6.0 m. A British shop unit is roughly 4.5 to 6 m of frontage, so 6.0 m is a generous single unit rather than a double. The two storey heights are trade_standard: a Victorian or Edwardian shop ground floor is tall (3.4 m to the underside of the first floor) and the flat above is not (2.8 m). DERIVED: eaves at 0.100 + 3.40 + 2.80 = 6.30 m above the road crown.

roof.note: trade_standard. A flat-topped frontage with a coped parapet, which is what a run of soot-blackened commercial terrace looks like when it is not slated. parapet_thickness_m is 0.215, DERIVED: it is the wall carrying on upward and a British brick is 215 mm long, so a one-brick parapet is 215 mm and not a round number. This is BOM line D7.

blocks.note: Soot brick per C3: this is the north-facing side of the street and it is the one that has had a hundred years of weather on it. Ground floor is plain wall with a side door, not a shopfront, because cam_B stands here and never photographs it.

SHOPS, ruled by Jafar 2026-09-22. This block was plain for one stated reason - "plain wall with a side door, not a shopfront, because cam_B stands here and never photographs it" - and that reason lapsed the day the hook camera moved onto this pavement: the block now fills the left third of the frame the whole stage is judged on, and the approved Hook sheet has a shop close on its near left with the street opening out beyond it. west_south stays PLAIN, so the contrast between the parade and the terraces survives and the street still changes as you walk down it. The 3.0 m between west_south's end at x=21.0 and this block's start at x=24.0 is the YARD ENTRANCE, and it is a gap in the data rather than a modelled object. It is what makes the dropped kerb above legitimate, and a dark slot in a terrace run is one of the cheapest night-frame reads there is.

roof.note: trade_standard, as the parade's: a slated pitch clear of the slate minimum.

blocks.note: THE SHIP CHANDLER'S, added 24 September as the measurement sitting's one new building. The plan names a chandler among the Hook's frontage uses (production/research/atlas-01/TOWN-FORM-BIBLE.md, D07/D08) and the street had none; a resident keeps 'a chandler's stall by the repair yard'. A building of its own, not a seventh bay: a 1.0 m passage separates it from the parade's north end at 39.0, its brick is the older grey of the far side rather than the parade's red, and its front is a metal refit (D06: 'Hook shops receive metal frames'). One 6.0 m bay on the parade's module and storey heights, so its levels line through with its neighbour's.

shopfront.note: trade_standard throughout. The four parts C5 names are stallriser, pilasters, fascia band and transom, and the fascia band's TOP is the underside of the first floor at 3.40 m, so fascia_bottom 2.85 gives a 0.55 m band. The side door leaf is 1981 x 838 mm, which is the standard British external door and is imperial (6 ft 6 in by 2 ft 9 in) because the country was in 1990. The shop door is wider. glazing_recess and the projections are what stop the frontage reading as one plane, which the M17.10 decomposition names as the cheap win. THE INTERIOR CARD is emitted as geometry only, in the held interior material: the lit back-wall artwork is BOM line C11, route GENERATE make_by 2D, and belongs to the decal generator rather than to this emitter.

facade.note: DERIVED reveal. A British brick is 215 x 102.5 x 65 mm, so a half-brick reveal is 102.5 mm exactly, and that is the number: a window flush with the wall reads as a decal, and the depth that fixes it is one brick on its side. brick_course_m is also arithmetic: 65 mm brick plus a 10 mm bed joint is 75 mm per course, which is the module every sill and lintel height on a real terrace is a whole number of. The window opening itself is trade_standard for a sash. C13_sills_lintels is the sill and lintel emitted here; they are one object with the window, not a separate pass.

chimney.note: trade_standard. A stack sits on the party wall between two houses and serves both, which is why a terrace roofline is a rhythm of stacks at the bay spacing and not a random scatter. 0.90 x 0.45 in plan is a two-flue stack. The POTS are BOM line D3, route HAVE (roll_top_chimney and weathertop_chimney, measured 0.67 and 0.95 m across), and are not emitted here.

aerial.note: DERIVED element length. British television in 1990 is UHF Bands IV and V, 470 to 860 MHz. A half-wave dipole at the 550 MHz middle of that band is c/(2f) = 299792458/(2 x 550e6) = 0.2725 m, so the elements of a domestic yagi are about 0.27 m and the whole comb is barely a metre across. That is why a period British roofline is a forest of small combs rather than the large dishes that replaced them. on_stacks names WHICH party-wall stacks carry one, so the count is a data choice and the BOM's count of 2 is met exactly.

gutter.note: trade_standard. 112 mm half-round is the standard British domestic gutter. Emitted as a run along the eaves with its fascia board, because the eaves shadow line is what stops a roof reading as a lid.

downpipe.note: trade_standard. 68 mm round is the standard British downpipe. art-direction calls the drainpipe the British answer to the American fire escape, and it is also the anchor the held Leaking005 stain decal wants: the pipe has to exist before the stain under it means anything. One per bay boundary, which is where a real one goes because it drains one roof slope into one gully.

column.note: MEASURED constraint, DERIVED spacing. The bill of materials records that the held lamp_post_01 measures 3.00 m, which is amenity height, and that a British residential lighting column of the period is roughly 5 to 6 m; 5.0 is the bottom of that measured bracket and the lantern height decides the whole night image. THE SPACING IS A RATIO, not a metre value: 4.0 x mounting height, so raising the column raises the spacing with it and the night frame stays lit the same way instead of turning into a row of pools. At 5.0 m that is 20 m, and over a 42 m street with alternating sides it puts FOUR lanterns in the scene, which is exactly the count BOM line H4 asks for. Change mounting_height and the count follows; that is the point.

lantern.note: DERIVED colour, and the derivation was run rather than recalled. art-direction R-B3 sources low pressure sodium as monochromatic at 589 nm with colour rendering index 0. Interpolating the CIE 1931 2-degree colour matching functions between 585 and 590 nm gives x=0.5467 y=0.4526 at 589 nm; through the sRGB D65 matrix that is linear (2.3766, 0.7055, -0.1351), which is outside the sRGB gamut on both ends, so it is clipped and normalised to a peak of 1 to give the linear triple above, and gamma-encoded to (1.000, 0.857, 0.000) or 255,219,0 in 8-bit. An emitter uses whichever of the two triples matches its colour space, and it must say which. range and intensity are NOT derived and are the first values of a series that has never been printed: they are the numbers the night frame will be tuned from once one exists, and rule 2 forbids calling them anything better than that.

window_practicals.colour_note: NOT derived, unlike the lantern above. This is the value StreetVignetteHost had hard-coded in its interior-light constructor on 2 September 2026, Color(1, 0.86, 0.62), moved into the shared file unchanged so both engines light a shop window the same warm tungsten and neither picks one by eye. Gamma-encoded sRGB, which is what a Unity Color literal means in a gamma project; an emitter in a linear project converts and says which it used. It is in the same never-printed class as the lantern range and intensity: rule 2 forbids calling it anything better than the first value of a series until a night frame exists to tune it from.
window_practicals.note: WHICH bays are lit is a data choice, so it is here rather than in either emitter. Three of six, because a parade at night with every unit lit is a shopping centre and a parade with none is a set. The intensities are in the same never-printed class as the lantern's.

sun.note: DERIVED. art-direction R-B1 places Meridian at 54 N and caps noon sun elevation at 59 degrees, which is the same statement: 90 - 54 + 23.44 = 59.4 is the midsummer noon maximum at that latitude. The equinox noon elevation at 54 N is 90 - 54 = 36.0 degrees exactly, and that is the value here, so the day condition is an ordinary spring or autumn British noon rather than a midsummer one. Azimuth 205 is judgement: just west of due south, so the light rakes ACROSS the street rather than down it and both cameras get a modelled facade instead of a flat one.

furniture.note: trade_standard silhouette: the British kiosk of this period is 3 ft square in plan and 8 ft 3 in tall, which is 0.914 and 2.515 m, and the proportion is the whole recognition. NO LETTERING AND NO CROWN ARE EMITTED, and that is canon rather than laziness: the bill of materials records that the crown and the operator lettering are real marks, that canon requires every brand fictional, and that nobody has yet written the Meridian operator into the brand bible. An unlettered kiosk is correct-and-incomplete; a lettered one would be a canon violation. That brand is a named next step.

trade_standard. The standard British cylindrical pillar box body is about 1.37 m tall and 0.60 m across. Same brand rule as the kiosk: NO CYPHER AND NO LETTERING is emitted. art-direction R-B4 counts the red boxes as the entire high-chroma accent budget of a British street, so between them the kiosk and this box carry the colour of the frame, and the wet night is where that matters.

trade_standard. 1.0 m is the normal British pedestrian guard rail height at a kerb. Three panels of 2.0 m starting at x=10.0, which puts them beside the gully at x=12.0. The held trunk_protection_railing is a TREE PIT GUARD and is a different object; the BOM says so explicitly and this is the line it says it about.

trade_standard, and imperial on purpose: the galvanised British dustbin of this period is about 18 in across and 24 in tall, which is 0.46 by 0.61 m. art-direction asks for these specifically and the BOM records that none of the four held bins is one, because all four are public street bins. Set back 1.60 m from the kerb, which is against the wall by the side door, because that is where a household bin waits.

double_yellow.note: trade_standard on the bands: a British double yellow is two 100 mm bands 100 mm apart, which is the dims field of BOM line A5 itself. COPIED, NOT RE-GUESSED, on the two numbers that are neither trade nor derived: the colour (0.78, 0.66, 0.18 gamma sRGB, worn municipal yellow rather than hazard yellow) and the 12 mm paint thickness both come from ledger/Assets/Scripts/Game/Furniture.cs BuildYellowLines, which has been painting the town's kerbs since M17.10. A second opinion about the same colour would put two yellows in one project. A5 is make_by 2D in the bill of materials and it ships as emitted paint at the colour above rather than as a decal; that is a route change on the same line and it is recorded here rather than left to be discovered. CORRECTED 2026-09-10 BY QUEUE 226: this note used to say that NO yellow-line image exists in this repository and that the six held RoadLines sets are worn WHITE paint. That is false of one of the six, and the refutation is a measurement rather than a sighting: ledger/Assets/StreamingAssets/Decals/ambientcg/RoadLines011_2K-PNG_Color.png is 2048x2048, its brightest one per cent means RGB 216.0/180.3/47.7, and its yellowness (the mean of red and green, less blue, over those pixels) is 150.5 against 3.4, -0.3, 4.6, 4.6 and 4.8 for RoadLines 001, 004, 007, 010 and 018, which are white. CC0 1.0, already recorded in that directory's THIRD-PARTY.md. THE ROUTE DOES NOT CHANGE WITH THE SENTENCE: paint_yellow is ProceduralOnly in AssetLibrary, so Unity renders it from the tint and ignores any pack file, and the Unreal probe paints it from the same tint, so binding that PNG on one engine and a tint on the other would render one surface from two different inputs. Whether to revisit ProceduralOnly on both engines together belongs on the quality ladder. The bands run the whole 42 m on both sides: real double yellows break at a crossover, and that break is a named next step rather than a thing this file pretends to have.

held_props.what: The meshes under ledger/Assets/Props/base-mesh that THIS street wants, placed by name. Every one is named by a line of production/specs/vignette-bill-of-materials.json; the bill of materials decides WHICH, and the directory listing decides nothing. 18 of the 39 held props are placed here in 40 instances, and the 21 that are not are listed in not_placed below with the reason, because a fetched prop that no line names is the failure this project keeps finding. THE COUNT MOVED ON 2026-09-10 AND THE TWO IT MOVED BY WERE AUTHORED HERE, not fetched: fascia_cornice_01 and fascia_console_01 are LEDGER's own geometry, written by production/art/fascia-01/author/make_fascia_mouldings.py and named by the bill of materials line C15_fascia_cornice_console. Until this change they sat in ledger/Assets/Props/base-mesh named by NOTHING, which is rule 6 exactly: built is not running.
held_props.dims_source: MEASURED, per prop, from the shipped .glb's own POSITION accessors walked through its node transforms (the same axis-aligned box glTFast hands Unity). dims_m is [along-x, up-y, across-z] in the glTF frame, which is the frame the piece list uses. These are NOT the numbers in content/props/manifest.json's measured block: that block describes the CLEANED LOD0 outputs, which are not in this repository, and it quotes Blender's z-up dims for the sources. Where the two agree they agree to a millimetre; where the pivot is concerned they do not agree at all, which is why the emitter aligns the loaded bounding box rather than trusting an origin.
held_props.pivot_note: THE SOURCE PIVOTS ARE NOT ALL AT THE BASE, measured: awning_02's origin is at its top-back (min y -1.318) because it hangs off a wall, poster and framed_poster are centred (min y -0.50 and -0.40), drainage_grate_01 hangs 15 mm below its origin, and the rest stand on it. So a placement here names where the prop's BOUNDING BOX CENTRE goes, exactly like every other piece in the list, and each emitter puts the loaded mesh's own bounds centre there. Nothing is ever scaled: the dims policy forbids inventing a size, and a prop that is the wrong size is a prop to replace, not to stretch.

place_kinds.ground: stands on whatever ground is under it. y comes from the section's own ground query at the prop's centre, plus half its measured height, and the footprint is probed for a datum like any other footed piece.
place_kinds.set_in: sits IN the ground rather than on it (the gully grate in its dish). ITS TOP FACE LIES IN THE RUNNING SURFACE AND TAKES THAT SURFACE'S CROSS-FALL, because a gully grate is the LID of its dish and water only reaches it if it is flush: the dish the ground query subtracts is added back, and the centre then drops half a thickness down the piece's own normal, which is the walk the ground slabs take. AMENDED 2026-09-09: before that this kind read same y as the ground query, which stood the grate on the dish floor and left it buried 10.25 to 20.00 mm under the channel and carriageway slabs, neither of which cuts a hole for it; the magnitude is in production/queue/162-the-grate-sits-under-the-channel-it-drains.md and the ruling is game-design/decision-2026-09-09-the-twelve-clauses-and-the-buried-grate.md section 3. The fall is taken from the section rather than from two ground samples, and it is the same reason this kind is deliberately NOT foot-probed: a grate straddles the step between carriageway, channel and kerb recess by design, so a foot probe over it reports a 40 mm gap that is the step and not a fault, and two samples a quarter of a metre apart would measure the kerb. A set_in prop over anything but the carriageway or the channel is refused by name rather than laid at a fall nobody measured.
place_kinds.wall: hangs on a frontage. The near face touches the building line, so the centre stands half its measured depth out from it, and y is either a centre height above the block base or the rule named in wall_y.
place_kinds.stack: stands on the top of a named chimney stack, which the roofline emitter records as it builds it so that no second opinion about the ridge height can exist.

held_props.yaw_rule: A wall prop faces the street: yaw 180 on the east frontage (the street is at -z from it) and yaw 0 on the west. Written per prop rather than derived, because the rule is about which way a MESH was modelled and that is a fact about the file, not about the street.

items.note: MANDATORY. The x and the 0.40 footprint are not chosen here: street.gully already carries them, and its own note records that 0.40 m is the MEASURED footprint of this exact mesh. The grate sits at the channel, half over the carriageway and half over the dish B3 emits, which is where a real gully grate sits.

MANDATORY, one pot per party-wall stack, which is five on the east parade. MEASURED CONFLICT, recorded rather than hidden: the pot is 0.674 m across and roofline.chimney.depth_m is 0.45, so the pot oversails the stack by 0.112 m on each side. Rescaling the mesh is forbidden by the dims policy and 0.45 m is the trade dimension for a stack serving two flues, so both numbers stand and the first cam_B frame is what decides whether this reads as a pot or as a lid. weathertop_chimney is EXCLUDED for the same measurement taken further: at 0.95 m across it oversails a 0.45 m stack by 0.25 m each side, more than half the stack again.

DRESSING. A bollard belongs where a vehicle can overrun a footway, so the pair stands at the two corners of the yard entrance the dropped kerb serves, not scattered along the parade. ONE DESIGN, REPEATED, which is what a council does; the other three held bollards stay inventory. This one because 1.008 m is the only held height in the British street bollard bracket (the others measure 0.79, 0.44 and 1.00, and the 1.00 is a plain square timber post).
The other corner of the yard entrance. west_south ends at x=21.0 and west_north starts at x=24.0, so 20.7 and 24.3 stand 0.3 m clear of each building corner.

DRESSING. Two public bins over 42 m of parade, one in each camera's near frame: this one is 4 m up the street from cam_A. Two and not four, because a British parade carries about one bin per shop group and the other two held bins are the same object at other sizes.

The far one, at the vanishing end of cam_A's kerb line. The flagship of the base-mesh set: Furniture.cs probes the whole prop pipeline with this key, so a run where this one is missing is a run where the pipeline is missing.

DRESSING, and it is the one placement that tells a small story: the yard is shut. Set across the mouth of the yard entrance at the back of the footway, which is where a barrier stands, and it is what makes the skip in the road and the clutter on the pavement one event rather than three unrelated props.
At the kerb by the skip. 0.45 m is a short cone and that is the measurement, not a choice.
The other end of the skip. Both cone models are held and both are on the same line, so the pair uses one each rather than one twice.

DRESSING. An A-board outside the fish market, turned so its two faces look up and down the pavement at the people who read them. What it CARRIES is BOM line G6 and is a decal, not this mesh; see the decals block.

DRESSING. The flyposting goes on the BLANK side of the street, which is the west: its ground floor is plain soot brick with a side door and no shopfront, and that is exactly the wall a bill gets pasted to. x=11.4 sits in the 0.95 m of blank wall between the side door at 10.5 and the first ground-floor window at 12.3, measured off this file's own bay layout.

DRESSING. The glazed case, further up the same blank wall, in the gap between west_north's side door at 25.5 and its first window at 27.3. A case gets a timetable and a wall gets a gig bill, which is why the two carriers carry different G6 images.

DRESSING, and the cheapest density on the list. Parked in the carriageway against the west kerb at the yard entrance, long axis along the street (yaw 90 turns the measured 3.31 m length up the road), 0.15 m off the kerb face. A builder's skip on the road outside a yard being cleared is a British street in one object, and it is the widest thing standing on the camber: 2.00 m across at 1 in 40 lifts its upslope corner 25 mm, which is arithmetic and not a placement fault.
On the pavement at the yard mouth, in front of the barrier.
One of two crates. The same model twice rather than two models once: a yard clears out its own crates, and they match.
The second crate, turned 20 degrees off the wall so the pair does not read as a shelf.

A barrel at the end of the row. Five clutter items from four of the eight held models; large_pallet, small_pallet, wooden_crate_02 and wood_barrel stay inventory because the yard mouth holds what fits in it.

DRESSING. Over the fish market, hung with its top at the underside of the fascia band, which is where a retractable awning is fixed. awning_02 AND NOT awning_01: the bill of materials says so in as many words, and the reason is measured (20 triangles and one LOD rung against 644 and three). It projects 1.735 m of its 2.0 m footway, which is what an awning does.
The second one, four bays up, so cam_B has one in frame and cam_A sees both in perspective. Two of six units, not six: a parade where every unit has its awning out is a parade nobody has looked at.

MANDATORY, one per bay, and the LENGTH IS THE DERIVED NUMBER RATHER THAN THE BAY. 5.8920 is 6.0000 (east_parade_fascia0.sx_m) less the 0.068 m D5 downpipe and twice the package's 0.0200 m clearance, because the five east downpipes stand on the party pilaster centres at x=9,15,21,27,33 and a 6.0000 run passes through all five. The run therefore stops 0.0200 m each side of every pipe and 0.0540 m short of each end of the terrace, which is what a real cornice does at a rainwater pipe. wall_centre_m 3.4750 stands its SOFFIT on the fascia band's top: the band is 2.95 to 3.50 in world with the 0.100 threshold on, so 0.100 + 3.4750 - 0.0750 = 3.5000 exactly. DERIVED PITCH: eye_height is measured from the FOOTWAY under the camera, not from y=0, so the emitter must read the ground it is standing on rather than assume a level. At a 60 degree vertical field a pitch of p degrees down puts the horizon at frame row 0.5 - tan(p)/(2 tan 30), so 4.0 degrees puts it at 0.439, just above the middle, which is where every British street reference in game-design/reference/ puts it. The same arithmetic set the RefTour pitch and is quoted here rather than re-derived.

The bill of materials' cam_B: from the far kerb, square to the frontage, roofline in frame. It stands on the WEST footway looking due east across the street at the east parade, at x=21.0 which is the middle of that block. DERIVED PITCH, and the negative sign means UP: the east eaves edge sits at 6.30 m with its 0.30 m overhang at z=4.825, so from an eye at 1.672 m and z=-4.0 the eaves is at atan((6.30-1.672)/8.825) = 27.7 degrees of elevation, which at a 60 degree vertical field is 0.908 of the half-frame and only just inside the top edge. Pitching up 3.0 degrees brings it to tan(24.7)/tan(30) = 0.796, clear of the edge, and still leaves the stallriser and the kerb in the bottom of the frame. This camera and only this camera sees the roofline, which is why D2, D4, D6 and D7 exist.

MOVED 23 SEPTEMBER TO THE APPROVED SHEET, and everything after this paragraph describes the RETIRED one. The numbers are the lens derived on 22 September from the pass 4 sheet's own geometry (production/reference/hook-sheet-lens.md) and built in tools/art-recipes/terrace-front.py: x -3.2, just south of the terrace end on the quay apron; z -2.2, 7.3 m from the east frontage; eye 2.0 m above the crown (1.9 m above the threshold: three people on the sheet read as 1.75 m adults); turned 20.4 degrees towards the parade, because the sheet's vanishing point is 478 px right of centre; fov 46 vertical. ONE THING IS NOT THE SAME: Blender holds the camera level and drops the horizon to 0.570 of the height with a lens shift, and this engine's camera has no shift, so it looks up 3.4 degrees instead, which puts the horizon at the same 0.570 and leans the verticals very slightly. From this commit the Unreal frame at this camera is the one paired with the sheet (Jafar, 23 September). RUNG 1 OF production/ladder.md: the viewpoint of the LOWER PANEL of production/art/atlas-01/concepts/hook.png on branch origin/art/atlas-01, so that the built street and the concept sheet can be judged side by side. Every number below was measured off that panel and is written with the measurement beside it; the panel content area is x 11 to 1012 and y 662 to 1278 of the 1024x1536 sheet, which is 1002 by 617 pixels, found by scanning for the white border rather than by eye. THE PANEL IS NOT A CONSISTENT PINHOLE PROJECTION and no exact camera can be derived from it: its right kerb, traced over 112 columns five pixels apart from x 420 to 975, departs from a straight line by 21.7 px at worst and 9.68 px rms, and a straight kerb in a true perspective is exactly straight. So the numbers below reproduce the panel's COMPOSITION from the robust quantities, and each one names its uncertainty. z_m -2.10: the panel's left gutter line has image slope (x - xv)/(y - yh) = -0.556 about its vanishing point, and for a ground line that ratio IS the lateral offset in camera heights, free of the focal length, so at 1.65 m the panel's camera stands 0.92 m from its left kerb; our west kerb face is at z = -3.0, giving z = -2.08, rounded to -2.10, which is 0.90 m from the kerb face and stands in the carriageway, not the channel (the channel starts at 2.745). eye_height_m 1.65: standing adult eye height, and the panel supports 1.65 to 1.9. Two independent reads: the light hatchback's rendered width of 60 px against its wheel contact 60 px below the horizon makes the camera height equal to the car's width, about 1.65 m; the man at the door, head top on the horizon at 1.75 m plus a 0.13 m kerb upstand, reads 1.88 m. The low end is taken because it is a human standing eye height and because this probe measures eye height from the ground under the camera, which here is the carriageway at y -0.0525. yaw_deg 11.0: the panel's street axis vanishes LEFT of centre, which for a pinhole camera can only be a rotation and never a position. Three traced lines put the vanishing column at 265, 330 and 401 of 1002, mean 332, which is 169 px left of centre; at the panel's derived focal length of 875 px that is 10.9 degrees, so the camera is turned 11 degrees toward the shopfront terrace. The spread of those three lines is 6.5 to 15.1 degrees and is the honest uncertainty. Positive yaw turns from +x toward +z, which puts the east parade on the right of frame as the panel puts its terrace. pitch_deg -2.6, and the sign means UP: the panel's horizon sits at row 348 of 617, which is 0.564 of the frame height and 0.128 half-heights BELOW centre, so the camera is pitched up. At a 39 degree vertical field, row = 0.5 - tan(p)/(2 tan(19.5)) puts the horizon at 0.5641 for p = -2.6 against the panel's 0.5640. The horizon row was read three ways that agree within 10 px: the car (348), the standing figures' eye level (350 to 358), and the traced ground lines. fov_vertical_deg 39.0: THE ONLY NUMBER HERE THAT NEEDS AN ASSUMPTION, because a single image fixes the scene only up to scale and every ratio in it is focal-length free; what pins the focal length is one LONGITUDINAL length. Two shopfront boundaries on the panel's right terrace sit 118 and 77 px below the horizon, and if the reference bay is 6.0 m (this street's own bay module, which is why it is the assumption made) the focal length is 875 px, giving 38.8 degrees vertical and 59.7 horizontal on the panel. If the reference bay is 5.0 m the vertical is 45 degrees and if it is 6.5 m it is 37; that is the uncertainty and it is stated rather than hidden. 39.0 vertical is taken so that the NEAR GROUND matches: the bottom edge of this frame lands 4.06 m ahead against the panel's 4.15 m, which is what sets the feel of standing there. The consequence is that at 1280x720 this probe converts 39.0 vertical to 64.4 degrees horizontal against the panel's 59.7, because the panel is 1.62 to 1 and this frame is 1.78 to 1 and no single number matches both axes of two different aspect ratios. x_m 4.0: the same station along the street as cam_A, so that the pair differs in the cross-street position and the look direction and in nothing else. At this station the east building line enters the right edge of frame 7.8 m ahead and the parade is seen from bay 2 to bay 6; the panel's terrace enters its right edge 5.9 m ahead, and the 1.9 m difference is NOT a camera error, it is this street being wider than the panel's (6.0 m carriageway and 2.0 m footways here against roughly 4 to 5 m and narrower there). No number above was moved to flatter the frame; the differences that remain are reported as findings.

THE CONDITION IS wet_night, the judged night condition, and not pin_setter_night: the two are identical in every field this reader takes, checked field by field in CoreTests, so either would render the same frames and the judged one is the one a settled reference is wanted FOR. exposure_pin stays 0.000 on both, held there by section 3 of game-design/decision-2026-09-10-ruling-the-exposure-ladder-and-the-sheet.md until 276 step 3 lands, and NO NIGHT PIN IS DERIVED FROM A DAY PIN BY ANY RATIO: that derivation is forbidden by name in that ruling, which records issuing and withdrawing it within an hour. light_probe is off on all six because the probe toggles every lantern and every practical and photographs each half, which is both the cost these rows cannot afford and the one thing a held condition must not have done to it between frames. WRITTEN HERE AND NOT YET READ WHERE IT MATTERS, as of 2026-09-16: Core reads it (StreetVignette.cs 1896) and writes it into vignette-pieces.json as false (lines 103 to 108), and no reader in ue-probe/ consumes it: the shot parser at VignetteSpec.h 526 to 533 reads id, camera and condition only, and ShouldProbeShot at VignetteShot.cpp 2790 reads the condition's lantern and practical flags, which are on for wet_night. Until the reader the 06:35Z ruling ordered in section 4 lands, a run carrying these rows probes all six, and by this note's own sentence the series it prints is not a settling series. SIX IS A COST CAP AND NOT A MEASURED SETTLING TIME: nothing has ever printed this series, so the run says NOT-SETTLED-WITHIN-6 when the series is still moving at row six, and 276 step 2 says that reading IS the finding and outranks the pin. WHAT THESE ROWS ALSO DID, AND WHY THEY ARE NOT THE FLOOR: they are six frames of identical applied input at one camera, and under the field-based fingerprint they join the four pinset_night rows into a night group of ten, larger than the day group of seven the noise floor had been read off. On 2026-09-16 that turned vignette-spec-test red on 6 of 555 checks, because the test asserts the floor is the reference cell's own family and the emitter chose by size. RULED in game-design/decision-2026-09-16-ruling-the-floor-is-read-in-a-family-that-holds-a-step-and-the-settle-rows-are-outside-it-by-their-own-fields.md: the floor is read off the largest identical-input group whose no-sky family holds a sky-only pair, because a spread with no step in its own family has nothing to be read against; the night family has one sky value and holds no pair, so these rows and the pinset rows are outside the floor by their own fields, and no key declares it. The line prints what size alone would have chosen (nullSeriesBySizeAlone), so the difference is on every run's line. These six sit after the null cell in the list, and the null cell stays the last shot of its own family, which is the separation its value comes from. Their own spread is the settle series, a reading of whether the night condition settles, printed as its own done-line key and never a floor.
lighting_grid_note: THREE REQUIRED FIELDS ON EVERY CONDITION: sun_intensity and sky_intensity, added 2026-09-09 by queue 205, and fog_max_opacity, added the same evening by section 4.4 of game-design/decision-2026-09-09-ruling-the-grid-not-the-ladder.md. All three were bare numbers inside the two emitters: the sun was the literal 3.0f at VignetteShot.cpp:1240, the sky was kSkyIntensityDay 1.0 or kSkyIntensityNight 0.35 picked by whether the sun was on, and the fog cap was const float kFogMaxOpacityWithSky = 0.45f. None was ever measured. THE VALUES CARRIED BY overcast_day AND wet_night ARE THE OLD LITERALS UNCHANGED, so this file moves where the numbers live and moves no number. Required rather than defaulted in both readers: a condition that does not name its sun, its sky or its fog cap refuses loudly instead of inheriting a value nobody chose. THE SUN LADDER IS RETIRED AND ITS SERIES IS PRESERVED IN SECTION 3 OF THAT RULING, which is the condition queue 206 set for removing it: five rungs at 3, 10, 30, 100 and 300 moved band.ground.p05 by 0.1243 across a HUNDREDFOLD of sun, against a null of 0.1172 measured between two shots of one condition, so the ladder measured 1.06 nulls and the rungs were rendered in increasing order, which confounds a drift in shot order with a response to the sun. WHAT REPLACES IT IS A GRID AT cam_hook: sky 1.00, 0.70, 0.50 and 0.35 crossed with sun 3, 10 and 30, twelve cells, interleaved so the shot order is not monotone in sky, plus ITS OWN NULL CELL (grid_null_repeat) shot last, plus SEVEN fog rows and three wetness rows at the reference cell (four rendered on 32bae70 and three more at 0.020, 0.050 and 0.080 added 2026-09-14 by section 2.5 of game-design/decision-2026-09-14-ruling-the-prune-is-gone-seven-is-a-floor-and-the-fog-is-the-cloud-deck.md, which also moved overcast_day's cap from 0.450 to 0.100 off that rendered series and crossed the new cap with sky 0.35, 0.50 and 0.70 in three further rows). EVERY ROW ADDED HERE IS A ONE-RUN PROBE ROW and the item that reads the run removes it: at about 1.67 MB of committed PNG per row per run, rows kept by default are rows nobody chose. NO CONSTANT IS SET FROM ANY OF THEM.
exposure_pin_note: QUEUE 219 AND 235, SET 2026-09-14, AND IT IS A CHOSEN RUNG RATHER THAN AN INTERPOLATION. Read off the printed ladder of run 41, committed at production/d1-probe/ue-vignette-verdict.txt whose line 1 names f6508b3: condition pin_030 at cam_hook came out at 0.6591 mean luma photographed after a night frame and 0.6590 photographed after a day frame, with clipHiAny 0/921600 and clipLoAll 0/921600 on both rows. It is the only photographed rung that lands in the 0.59 to 0.62 band this rig's own auto exposure settled to on the six day frames of that run that did not follow darkness, so pinning here moves no frame far from the level the resident has been judging. Rung 0.030 is refused by its own row, which held its pin perfectly and blew 206373 of 921600 pixels while doing it. Rungs 3.000 and 10.000 held at 0.1892 and 0.0610, both far below that band. WHAT THIS VALUE IS NOT: a photometric match to the reference street photograph, which reads 0.4102 on this project's ruler and sits between rungs 0.300 and 3.000. The value is HELD at 0.300 through D28 step 2 by the ruling of 2026-09-14 (game-design/decision-2026-09-14-ruling-the-pin-belongs-to-the-rig-and-the-render-waits-for-it.md), so that the sky and sun series are read at one exposure; a finer ladder inside the 0.300 to 3.000 bracket is re-raised only with that series printed, and no number here was interpolated toward the reference's 0.4102.

not_emitted_from_this_file.why: Its own IF-IN-FRAME condition is a pedestrian crossing, and this scene has no crossing. The dropped kerb here is a yard entrance, which is a different thing. Emitting a beacon without a crossing would be a beacon standing next to nothing.

Its condition is a metered frontage, and this frontage is not one. BOM line A5 makes DOUBLE YELLOW LINES mandatory the length of this kerb, and double yellows mean no waiting at any time: a parking meter on the same stretch is a contradiction on the road surface. Excluded on the scene's own evidence rather than on cost.
Its condition is a stop in frame. A 42 m vignette 10 m wide between building lines has no room for a stop without the shelter becoming the subject.
